title: Mother of the Captive, May Rain Water You
intro: The heading in Abu Firas al-Hamdani’s diwan says his mother died while he was a captive of the Byzantines. He asks for rain on her grave, then imagines a messenger arriving with news of his ransom and finding her gone. He calls on the days she fasted, the nights she spent in prayer and the people she sheltered to mourn her in his absence. In the last verse he finds comfort in the thought that he will follow her.

translation: Mother of the captive, may rain water you.
How it grieved you, what the captive suffered.
1.sharh: Rain on a grave is a blessing for the dead. Her son calls himself the captive twice, first to name her and then to recall whose suffering she felt as her own.

translation: Mother of the captive, may rain water you,
bewildered rain that neither stays nor goes.
2.sharh: The qualifying verb carries over from the preceding half. Even the rain seems to hesitate at the grave, as a mourner might linger and still have to leave.

translation: Mother of the captive, may rain water you.
To whom can the bearer bring word of ransom now?
3.sharh: Ransom once meant two things, release for the prisoner and good news for his mother. His return is still possible, but the messenger has lost the person he meant to tell.

translation: Mother of the captive, for whose sake are braids
and long locks tended now that you are dead?
4.sharh: The question hangs over the break until the second half names the locks. Letting hair grow and tending it once gave someone else the pleasure of seeing him.

translation: When your son travels over land and sea,
who prays for him or asks protection for him?
5.sharh: Land and sea put the whole width of the journey between mother and son. She could still accompany him by asking God to keep him safe.

translation: He may never close his eyes in peace.
It would be mean of him to let joy visit.
6.sharh: He speaks of himself as the absent son. Sleep comes under a prohibition, and even a passing visit from happiness would amount to disloyalty.

translation: You have tasted calamity and death,
with neither child beside you nor companion.
7.sharh: To taste death makes it something her body underwent. The son imagines the empty spaces at her side where the closest members of a household should have stood.

translation: The one your heart loved was missing from a place
where the angels of heaven were present.
8.sharh: He names himself through her affection. The angels can attend the dying woman, which makes the one familiar face missing from the gathering all the more palpable.

translation: Let every day you fasted weep for you.
You held out as the midday heat grew fierce.
9.sharh: The first witnesses he calls are the days themselves. A fast means going without water, and noon in the heat measures what her quiet perseverance cost.

translation: Let every night you stood in prayer weep for you.
You prayed till the bright dawn broke.
10.sharh: Her nights take their place beside her days. Standing means standing to pray, and the arrival of light tells us how long she stayed there.

translation: Let every frightened, persecuted soul weep for you,
whom you sheltered when protectors were scarce.
11.sharh: Now people are summoned as mourners. Granting protection was a public undertaking to stand behind someone in danger, particularly costly when nobody else would do it.

translation: Let every poor, destitute soul weep for you,
whom you helped when no marrow was left in the bone.
12.sharh: A whole history of hunger contracts into the hollow of a bone. The poet gives the beneficiary of her help a body, where a bare list of virtues might have said only that she gave alms.

translation: Mother, how many a long grief
passed over you with no one to help you bear it.
13.sharh: “Mother” replaces “mother of the captive”. After naming the people she sustained, he considers how much she endured without that same help herself.

translation: Mother, how many a secret, kept safe
in your heart, died there and will never come to light.
14.sharh: A secret seems to have lived a second life inside hers. Her discretion was so complete that he can mourn what disappeared with her without knowing what it was.

translation: Mother, how often news that I was near
reached you, with your short span barring the way.
15.sharh: The messages did reach her. The distance that mattered in the end was the time left to her, too short for welcome news to become a meeting.

translation: To whom can I complain, with whom can I speak privately,
when hearts can no longer hold what is in them?
16.sharh: Complaint calls for a listener, confidential speech for someone trusted. In the image a chest has only so much room for what must be told.

translation: Whose prayer will keep harm from me now?
By the light of whose face shall I see my way?
17.sharh: Her prayer could reach him in captivity. The light of her face belongs to the ordinary intimacy of being in the same room, a second kind of protection.

translation: Through whom can the full stroke of fate be warded off?
Who can open a way through hardship for me?
18.sharh: He imagines a blow turned aside and a closed way opened. The mother is the person through whose prayers relief might come, even when events themselves are beyond her power.

translation: What consoles us for losing you is that soon
we too shall go where you have gone, in the life to come.
19.sharh: He draws comfort from the very mortality that took her. The same verb is given first to the dead woman and then to the living who will follow her.

1.1.4-5.head: سَقاكِ غَيث
1.1.4-5.meaning: “May rain water you.” A blessing spoken over a dwelling or a grave.

1.2.1.head: كُره
1.2.1.meaning: Sorrow or distress at something unwelcome. She keenly felt what befell her son.

2.2.1.meaning: To be at a loss which way to go. The rain itself hesitates.

3.2.3.head: فِدى
3.2.3.meaning: Ransom, the price paid to free someone. The long form is shortened in the verse.

3.2.5.head: بَشير
3.2.5.meaning: A bearer of welcome news, here the imagined messenger announcing release.

4.2.3.head: ذُؤابَة
4.2.3.meaning: A hanging lock or braid of hair.

4.1.5.head: رَبّى
4.1.5.meaning: To let something grow and tend it. The locks are what is tended.

5.2.5.head: اِستَجارَ
5.2.5.meaning: To seek protection, here on another person’s behalf.

6.1.4-5.head: قَرير العَين
6.1.4-5.meaning: “With cool eyes.” At peace, able to rest without anxiety.

6.2.3.head: أَلَمَّ
6.2.3.meaning: To pay a brief visit. Joy is an occasional guest.

7.1.3.head: رَزِيَّة
7.1.3.meaning: Calamities, especially the loss of someone dear. The reciter follows the Tunis manuscript in placing calamity before death. Al-Dahhan prints the two in reverse order.

7.2.5.head: عَشير
7.2.5.meaning: A close companion, often a spouse or member of the household.

8.2.4.head: حُضور
8.2.4.meaning: Those in attendance. The plural sets the angels beside the one absent son.

9.2.1.head: مُصابَرَة
9.2.1.meaning: Holding out against a hardship, here the thirst of a fast.

10.1.4-5.head: قامَ اللَّيل
10.1.4-5.meaning: “Stood the night.” To spend the night in prayer.

11.2.1.head: أَجارَ
11.2.1.meaning: You granted him sanctuary. The vowel before the final pronoun is extended.

11.2.3-4.head: عَزَّ المُجير
11.2.3-4.meaning: “A protector was hard to find.” The reciter follows the Tunis manuscript. Al-Dahhan prints «قلّ المجير», “protectors were few”.

12.2.1.head: أَغاثَ
12.2.1.meaning: You came to his aid at a moment of desperate need.

12.2.5.head: رير
12.2.5.meaning: The thin marrow of a bone. Even that last reserve is gone.

13.2.6.head: نَصير
13.2.6.meaning: Someone who stands by another person in distress.

14.1.5.head: مَصون
14.1.5.meaning: Kept inviolate, here in the confidence of a single person.

15.2.2.head: دون
15.2.2.meaning: Standing between the news and its fulfilment.

16.1.5.head: ناجى
16.1.5.meaning: To speak in confidence, with a trusted listener.

17.1.3.head: داعِيَة
17.1.3.meaning: A woman who prays, here his mother interceding for him.

17.1.4.head: وَقى
17.1.4.meaning: To be shielded against harm, here through her prayer.

18.1.2.head: اِستَدفَعَ
18.1.2.meaning: To seek to ward something off.

18.1.4.meaning: Dealt out in full, as one's allotted fate.

19.2.5.meaning: The life to come, where he hopes to join her.
